vulnerabilities.title: STACK_BUFFER_OVERFLOW via unbounded strcpy of environment variables to fixed-size stack buffers in main()

root_cause.description: main() copies three attacker-controlled environment variables (TARGET_APPIMAGE, APPIMAGE, APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN) to fixed-size stack buffers (0x1000 = 4096 bytes each) using strcpy() without any length validation. Environment variables on Linux can be arbitrarily long (up to 128KB by default). The stack frame has no canary (confirmed: no __stack_chk_fail in symbols, no canary instructions). The binary is not PIE (fixed base 0x400000) and has no RELRO (GOT fully writable). All three strcpy calls share the same root cause: unbounded strcpy of an environment variable to a fixed-size stack buffer with no bounds checking.

data_flow: getenv('TARGET_APPIMAGE') at 0x4054a4 returns attacker-controlled string
If set: strcpy([rbp-0x6030], getenv_result) at 0x4054d9 — no length check, buffer is 0x1000 bytes
If not set: strcpy([rbp-0x6030], '/proc/self/exe') at 0x4054ba (fixed string, safe)
getenv('TARGET_APPIMAGE') again at 0x4054e3, result used as source for strcpy([rbp-0x5030], ...) at 0x4054f2 — no length check, buffer is 0x1000 bytes
getenv('APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN') at 0x405517, if non-NULL: strcpy([rbp-0x4030], getenv_result) at 0x405535 — no length check, buffer is 0x1000 bytes
Overflow from [rbp-0x6030] reaches return address after 0x6038 = 24632 bytes
Overflow from [rbp-0x5030] reaches return address after 0x5038 = 20536 bytes
Overflow from [rbp-0x4030] reaches return address after 0x4038 = 16440 bytes

security_check.expected: Length of environment variable value should be validated against buffer size (0x1000 = 4096 bytes) before copying, or strncpy/snprintf should be used instead of strcpy
security_check.actual: No length check whatsoever. strcpy() is called directly with the getenv() return value as source and a fixed-size stack buffer as destination
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing length validation on all three strcpy calls. No stack canary to detect overflow. No FORTIFY_SOURCE (no __*_chk functions in GOT/PLT).

vulnerable_operation.operation: strcpy to fixed-size stack buffer without length check
vulnerable_operation.expression: strcpy([rbp-0x6030], getenv("TARGET_APPIMAGE")); strcpy([rbp-0x5030], getenv("TARGET_APPIMAGE")); strcpy([rbp-0x4030], getenv("APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN"))
vulnerable_operation.target: stack buffers at rbp-0x6030, rbp-0x5030, rbp-0x4030 (each 0x1000 = 4096 bytes)
vulnerable_operation.size: unbounded (source is getenv() return value, no length limit)

impact.reason: An environment variable value longer than 4096 bytes overflows the stack buffer, corrupting adjacent stack data including other buffers, saved registers (r15/r14/r13/r12/rbx), saved rbp, and the return address. No canary prevents this. The overflow is contiguous from the buffer to the return address.
Overflowing the stack buffer corrupts saved registers and return address, causing SIGSEGV when the function returns or when corrupted register values are used.

evidence.description: strcpy([rbp-0x6030], getenv("TARGET_APPIMAGE")) — disassembly shows 'lea rdi,[rbp-0x6030]; mov rsi,rax; call strcpy' at 0x4054cf-0x4054d9. No length check precedes the call. Buffer is 0x1000 bytes (from rbp-0x6030 to rbp-0x5030).
strcpy([rbp-0x5030], getenv("TARGET_APPIMAGE")) — disassembly shows 'lea rdi,[rbp-0x5030]; call strcpy' at 0x4054eb-0x4054f2. No length check. Buffer is 0x1000 bytes (from rbp-0x5030 to rbp-0x4030).

strcpy([rbp-0x4030], getenv("APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN")) — disassembly shows 'lea rdi,[rbp-0x4030]; mov rsi,rax; call strcpy' at 0x40552b-0x405535. No length check. Buffer is 0x1000 bytes (initialized with rep stos of 0x3fe dwords = 0xff8 bytes at 0x4054f7-0x405510, plus 8 bytes for '/tmp' prefix).

main() prologue: 'push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r15; push r14; push r13; push r12; push rbx; sub rsp,0x6438' — no canary setup (no fs:[0x28] read, no __stack_chk_fail call). Stack frame is 0x6438 + 40 bytes of saved registers.

S1 confirms: no stack canary (F004), no PIE (F005, base 0x400000), no RELRO (F003, GOT writable), no FORTIFY (F007). These facts mean the overflow is undetectable at runtime, return addresses are at fixed offsets, and GOT entries are writable.

verification_required: Confirm that the binary is invoked in a context where environment variables are attacker-controlled (e.g., setuid, service wrapper, or direct user invocation)
Verify that the overflow reaches the return address without hitting any unmapped pages first (the 0x6038-byte overflow distance is within the stack's mapped region)
Confirm the exact behavior when TARGET_APPIMAGE is not set but argv[0] is used instead (argv[0] is also attacker-controlled but typically shorter)

vulnerabilities.title: LIBRARY_HIJACKING via dlopen of libfuse.so.2 and libnotify.so.3-8 without RPATH/RUNPATH

root_cause.description: The binary loads external libraries via dlopen() without any RPATH or RUNPATH set in the ELF. The library search order is LD_LIBRARY_PATH > /etc/ld.so.cache > default paths. An attacker who controls LD_LIBRARY_PATH or can place files in the current working directory (when LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes '.' or is unset but CWD is in the search path) can substitute a malicious libfuse.so.2 or libnotify.so.3-.so.8. The malicious library's .init_array/.init section executes immediately upon dlopen, before any dlsym resolution. The binary performs no integrity verification (no checksum, no signature) on the loaded libraries.

global have_libloaded (0x62aee0, .bss) — flag set after dlopen
GOT entries for dlopen (0x62ad68) and dlsym (0x62ad88) — writable (no RELRO)

security_check.actual: dlopen() is called with bare library names ('libfuse.so.2', 'libnotify.so.3') and no RPATH/RUNPATH. No integrity verification is performed on the loaded library.

vulnerabilities.title: SQUASHFS_PARSER_ATTACK_SURFACE — attacker-controlled file format data processed by sqfs_* parsing functions without comprehensive validation

root_cause.description: The binary processes squashfs filesystem images embedded in AppImage files. The squashfs parsing functions (sqfs_open_image, sqfs_init, sqfs_traverse_open, sqfs_traverse_next, sqfs_inode_get, etc.) read and process attacker-controlled file format data including superblock fields, inode table entries, directory entries, and data block descriptors. The offsets and sizes from the superblock are used to compute file positions for further reads. While basic magic and version checks exist, the full extent of validation on sizes, offsets, and counts read from the squashfs image is unclear and requires deeper analysis of all sqfs_* functions.

global elf_size (0x62ae98) — used as offset into AppImage file for squashfs payload
